slides.title: EES has replaced passport stamps at Schengen borders
slides.body: What to know before a short stay in Europe.

slides.title: Every border crossing is recorded digitally
slides.body: EES registers each entry and exit of non-EU nationals on a short stay at the Schengen external border. It applies whether or not you need a visa.

slides.title: Fingerprints and a facial image, no stamp
slides.body: The digital record has replaced passport stamping. Ireland and Cyprus are not in the Schengen Area, so their borders work differently.

slides.title: Not every day in Europe counts
slides.body: Days spent on an EU residence permit or a long-stay (D) visa are not part of the 90/180 short-stay count.

slides.title: Check your own dates
slides.body: Enter your trips and see how many days you have left and when you can go back.

caption:
Since 10 April 2026, the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) records every entry and exit of non-EU nationals on a short stay at the Schengen external border, with fingerprints and a facial image. It applies whether or not you need a visa, and it has replaced passport stamps.

Worth knowing: days spent on an EU residence permit or a long-stay (D) visa do not count towards the 90/180 short-stay limit.
